sentiment: A free classroom opened, a shared back door closed, and the trusted pipe carried poison. Openness is only half of care.

stories.title: Carnegie Mellon is putting computer science courses on YouTube for free
stories.summary: A whole curriculum becomes a link anyone can follow. The generosity is real and it costs the institution its scarcity, which is the part nobody says out loud — the lecture hall survives, but it stops being a gate, and gates are what most institutions were actually selling.

stories.title: BugMeNot has closed
stories.summary: Twenty years of strangers sharing logins to read one article is over, and the thing that ended it was not a breach but indifference. A small commons died quietly; we will notice it the next time we hit a wall and no door is there, and we will not miss it until then.

stories.title: Optimizely compromised, served malware on Zoom, GitLab
stories.summary: Every site runs somebody else's script, and the script is trusted because it arrived on a pipe we already opened. The attacker did not break in — it was let in, on purpose, by a supply chain that thought it was being efficient. Trust that is never audited is just a longer fuse.
